name: atomicmax
algorithm: t workers (Mk: tasks; Go: goroutines; C, Rust and Zig: OS threads) each take a ticket n times with a relaxed fetch-and-add on one shared 64-bit counter, then raise one shared 64-bit maximum to the ticket with a weak compare-exchange loop (relaxed, relaxed): Mk atomic.Atomic[i64] FetchAdd and CompareExchangeWeak, C11 atomic_fetch_add_explicit and atomic_compare_exchange_weak_explicit, Rust AtomicI64 fetch_add and compare_exchange_weak, Zig std.atomic.Value(i64) fetchAdd and cmpxchgWeak (.monotonic), Go atomic.Int64 Add and CompareAndSwap (Go has no orders and no weak CAS). Prints the counter and the maximum, t * n and t * n - 1 (README.md).

models.c: OS threads, C11 <threads.h> and <stdatomic.h> explicit orders

no_counts: B24 does not apply: the counter and the maximum show every operation happened
notes: Written by std-sync2's rerun for atomic.Atomic[T] (D-380, D-382): the ordered, generic atomic against each language's own, at the same orders (Go has only sequentially consistent atomics and a strong CAS, which on x86-64 compile to the same lock-prefixed instructions).
